english.title: Without authority disclose information re content / sender / addressee of message obtained by wireless telegraphy
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), without the authority of a designated person, disclosed information as to the contents, sender or addressee of a message which was obtained using wireless telegraphy apparatus and of which neither you nor a person on whose behalf you were acting was an intended recipient
english.legislation: Contrary to section 48(1)(b) and (4) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006.

english.notes:
(i) Section 48(1)(a) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 provides that it is irrelevant whether the message was sent by means of wireless telegraphy or not.
(ii) Section 48(5) of the Act provides that designated person means the Secretary of State, the Commissioners for His Majesty's Revenue and Customs, or any other person designated for the purposes of this section by regulations made by the Secretary of State.
(iii) Section 48(2) of the Act provides that the offence is only committed if the information disclosed by the person is information that would not have come to his/her knowledge but for the use of wireless telegraphy apparatus by him/her/another person.
(iv) Section 48(4) of the Act provides that the offence is not committed if the person discloses information in the course of legal proceedings or for the purpose of legal proceedings.
(v) Section 105 of the Act makes special provisions for this offence in relation to ships and aircraft.
(vi) Section 107 of the Act provides for proceedings and enforcement regarding this offence.
(vii) Section 110 of the Act provides for criminal liability of company directors, managers, etc.
(viii) The Wireless Telegraphy (Fixed Penalty) Regulations 2011, (In force 01/10/2011), introduces a £100-00p fixed penalty charge for summary only offences under the Act, as from that date. This regime does not include offences relating to illegal broadcasting (pirate radio).
(ix) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.
english.standardstatementoffacts: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant, without the authority of a designated person, disclosed information as to the contents, sender or addressee of a message which was obtained using wireless telegraphy apparatus and of which neither the defendant nor a person on whose behalf the defendant was acting was an intended recipient.

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Fixed Penalty charge of £100-00p (in force from 01/10/2011).

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
